critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical product of two canonical published anomalies (earnings-to-price and the Sloan accrual measure, here in its CFO-minus-earnings form), so it rediscovers "quality-adjusted value" rather than testing a new interaction, and the rank-product construction adds no economic content beyond the two known legs.

Book-to-market interacted with gross profits-to-assets is precisely the combination Novy-Marx (2013) published and marketed as the canonical profitability-plus-value strategy, making this a direct rediscovery.

Beyond being Piotroski's positive-CFO screen applied to B/M, the INDICATOR collapses all negative-CFO firms to exactly zero, so they pool indistinguishably with genuine growth (low B/M) names in the short leg and the resulting spread is not the stated "value within cash-generating firms" comparison.

The enterprise-value construction is correctly specified and the leverage gate on EBITDA yield is a defensible, less-trodden variant than the standard B/M-times-profitability composites, though it overlaps materially with quality/safety-plus-value (QMJ) and the ratio is non-monotone for firms with negative EV or negative EBITDA, which should be handled before testing.

Sales-to-price conditioned on a five-year net-margin trend is the most substantive interaction in this batch and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the margin-improvement leg echoes Piotroski's Δmargin component and the 5-period TREND on annual data will bite into coverage and tilt toward long-lived survivors — worth checking coverage before crediting any alpha.

Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa and Nikolaev already showed that the return predictability in book-to-market comes essentially entirely from its retained-earnings component, so scaling B/M by RE/AT is a rediscovery of a documented decomposition rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.

A coherent value × short-term cash-coverage conditional that is close to (but not identical with) the well-known Piotroski-style value-plus-financial-soundness combination, and the RANK([0,1]) × signed IND_ZSCORE construction means high B/M with negative coverage produces the most negative scores — an acceptable but worth-checking implementation of the intended conditioning.

The two legs are mechanically entangled (cash sits in `act`, so high cash mechanically depresses `lct/act`), making this largely a repackaged cash-to-price / current-ratio combination rather than an informative interaction.

Sales-to-price and leverage-change are each individually well-documented, but conditioning cheap revenue on a three-year deleveraging trend is a defensible value-trap screen with a hypothesis that matches the expression's direction.

Penalizing `dp/at` inside an EBITDA/EV signal is close to mechanically converting the ratio back toward the standard EBIT/EV multiple, so the "interaction" is largely a trivial redefinition of an already-published enterprise-multiple anomaly.

Value conditioned on working-capital stability is a reasonable and distinct construct, though the ABS operator discards the signed accrual information that the accrual anomaly says is the economically relevant part, weakening the stated "deteriorating fundamentals" rationale.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Gross-Margin Stability Sales Value signal — same value leg and same margin ratio with VOL swapped for TREND — and it offers no diagnosis of why that signal's FMB slope and FF5 alpha had opposite signs.

This is a pure recombination of two archive signals — the cash-to-market anchor from "Liability-Maturity Adjusted Cash Discount" times the exact oancf/lct overlay from "Current-Claim Cashflow Book Value" — with no new variable or mechanism, so it adds essentially no independent information beyond what has already been tested.

Economically coherent yield-trap screen with a genuinely new variable (dvc) and internally consistent signs, though dvc entering both legs makes part of the interaction mechanical and the non-payer mass will compress the first rank into a large tie block that limits effective coverage.

The EBITDA-to-price anchor is new to this archive and the sign logic is consistent, but the overlay is the third variation on "penalize rising balance-sheet-to-sales ratios," a family that has already produced fmb_tstat of 0.295 and 1.612, so the prior is weak.

This is a minimal edit of the archived "Working-Capital Discipline Book Value" (drop ABS, swap sale for revt) and sits directly between it and "Working-Capital Buildup Penalized Sales Value," so it reads as a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different response to the earlier wrong-signed alpha.

Depreciation intensity is a genuinely new overlay dimension and the direction is internally consistent, but dp/revt is largely a technology/industry characteristic that IND_ZSCORE will partly neutralize, leaving a thin economic link to whether cash-to-price cheapness is real.

Well-diagnosed response to the earlier sales-yield failure — it replaces the distress-prone cheap-sales anchor with cash-flow yield and uses a coverage ratio that is related to but not redundant with the archived oancf/lct overlay — with hypothesis, expression, and expected sign all aligned.

This collapses the archive's cash-value interactions into a single dimensionally incoherent ratio (subtracting a flow, depreciation, from stocks of cash and current liabilities) and is otherwise a rediscovery of the well-known net-cash/net-current-asset-to-price value measure with no genuine cross-theme structure.

Internally consistent and correctly signed, and the static retained-earnings-to-liabilities overlay is economically distinct from the archive's flow-based dividend coverage signal, though it remains an incremental variation on the same dividend-yield-times-solvency template and is close to the known retained-earnings/distress-conditioned value literature.

The anchor switch from sales yield to earnings yield is a substantive, well-diagnosed response to the archive's sign conflict (cheap revenue loading on distressed low-margin firms) and the expression matches the hypothesis, though margin-stability-conditioned earnings yield sits near the established quality-value/earnings-stability literature and the 3-period VOL term will further thin already low coverage.

This is the archive's best-performing Maintenance-Light Cash Value with only the value anchor swapped and an identical overlay, so it reads as a cosmetic variant rather than a diagnosed improvement, and the overlay is partly mechanical since depreciation is added back inside oancf.

Conditioning high book-to-market on an improving retained-earnings-to-liabilities trend is effectively Piotroski's value-plus-financial-strength strategy (rising profitability plus falling leverage) rediscovered, and retained earnings is itself a component of the ceq numerator, creating mechanical overlap with the value anchor.

Expression, hypothesis, and expected sign are mutually consistent with adequate coverage, and net working capital scaled by total liabilities is a genuinely different liquidity overlay from the archive's cash-flow-coverage and current-liability-change variants, though it is close to the Altman-style distress screen and to the broader distress-conditioned value idea.

This is a straight leg-swap between two archived signals — the che/market value leg from "Operating-Quality Backed Cash Discount"/"Liability-Maturity Adjusted Cash Discount" combined with the exact gross-profit-over-lct quality leg from "Gross-Profit Claim Covered Cashflow Yield" — so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The economics are coherent (cheap cash is only credible if residual post-dividend cash flow covers creditor claims), but the construction is again a two-way recombination of archived pieces — the (oancf−dvc)/liabilities leg from "After-Payout Liability Cover Yield" with the cash-to-market value leg — differing only by lct→lt, which is unlikely to generate independent evidence.

The level of the short-term liability share as a conditioner on cash-flow yield is distinct from the archived change-in-lct/lt trap signal and the expression matches the stated positive-sign hypothesis, though lct/lt is heavily industry- and business-model-driven and the value leg is a standard cash-flow-to-price anomaly, so the incremental content is modest.

Internally consistent (high payout yield × rising liabilities loads high, predicted negative) and not a direct archive rediscovery, but the liability-growth leg is close to the well-documented net debt issuance/asset growth anomaly, and dvc/market has a large mass of tied zeros for non-payers that will blunt the RANK leg.

This is essentially the archived "Net-Current-Asset EBITDA Yield" with ni substituted for ebitda — a numerator swap on an already-tested signal whose FMB slope came out significantly opposite to the expected sign, so it re-tests a known contradiction rather than diagnosing it.

It stacks the archived EBITDA/EV multiple with two previously tested quality legs whose components share the same lct scaling, making the SUMRANK largely redundant and the whole construct an incremental variant of "Cash-Covered EBITDA Enterprise Value" and "Liability-Maturity Adjusted Cash Discount".

The quality leg (oancf − ni) is the canonical Sloan accruals anomaly merely rescaled by total liabilities, and the composite is a near-cosmetic variant of the archive's already-tested cash-to-market × operating-cash-quality signals (Operating-Quality Backed Cash Discount, Self-Financed Cash Discount).

The quality leg (oancf − dp)/lt is byte-for-byte the one already tested in "Maintenance-Covered Earnings Yield," so this is a leg-swap recombination of two archived signals (that one and "After-Payout Liability Cover Yield") rather than a new mechanism.

It is internally consistent and genuinely motivated by the fmb/alpha sign conflict in the earlier net-current-asset EBITDA signal by replacing a liquidity-buffer reward with a cash-conversion efficiency test, though the act + lct denominator is an ad hoc gross-working-capital scalar whose economic interpretation is weaker than net working capital or sales.

This repeats the already-tested "Accelerating-Asset-Wear Book Trap" / depreciation-intensity theme with only a level-vs-acceleration and denominator change, and scaling dp by gross profit (which can be near zero or negative) makes the conditioning variable numerically unstable despite winsorization.

It is a component swap inside the archive's best-performing construction (che-to-market × SUMRANK quality composite), substituting ni/revt for oancf/revt and re/lt for −cogs/revt, both of which already appear as quality legs elsewhere in the archive, so it tests no new economic channel.

The expression matches the stated negative-sign hypothesis and pairs a sales-yield anchor with a post-maintenance cash-burn leg not previously combined in the archive, but the "trap" framing is largely presentational since the leg is just the sign-flipped coverage ratio proposed elsewhere in this same batch, making the two proposals partially redundant.

This is a cosmetic variant of the already-tested "Maintenance-Light Cash Value" — the only change is RANK→IND_RANK on the identical base and an identical overlay — so it cannot deliver a substantively different economic test.

The base is essentially a free-cash-flow-to-price value proxy (close to published FCF/P), but the pairing with a cash-to-total-liabilities creditor-protection overlay is a coherent and not-yet-tested combination whose stated sign matches the expression's direction.

The oancf/ebitda conversion ratio flips sign whenever EBITDA is negative (a non-trivial share of firms), so the overlay will systematically mislabel loss-makers as poor converters or vice versa, and the second leg (−lct/revt) simply reuses the already-tested liability-intensity overlay.

Economically sensible refinancing-risk conditioner that is distinct from the prior lct/lt overlays by isolating interest-bearing short-term debt, though dlc already enters the enterprise-value denominator so the two legs partially double-count the same variable.

Direct rediscovery of the archived "Cash-Cushion Profit Persistence" with only ni swapped for oancf in the smoothed coverage overlay, and the oancf/lct coverage state was itself already tested in two other archived signals.

Because lct typically dwarfs oancf, the overlay (lct−oancf)/revt is dominated by short-term liability intensity rather than "cash burn," making it a sign-flipped recombination of the already-tested lct/sale overlay rather than the new cash-coverage test the hypothesis claims.

Using the worst recent cash-conversion realization rather than a level or mean is a substantively different (downside-floor) conditioner within a heavily mined cash-yield family, and the expression matches the stated hypothesis and sign, though the marginal information over the archived MA/level versions is likely small.

This is a cosmetic level→TREND swap on the archived "Cost-Scaled Cash Conversion EBITDA Yield," and the archive already demonstrates that this exact transformation destroys performance (Operating-Quality Backed Cash Discount fmb 3.24 vs. Improving-Operations Cash Discount fmb 0.77).

The quality leg (revenue per unit of act+lct) is a genuinely different channel — capital productivity rather than cash coverage or cash conversion — from the many prior che/market interactions, though it is the Nth instance of the same template and the "working-capital base" is really a crude scale proxy (assets *plus* liabilities) rather than net working capital, so the economic interpretation is looser than the hypothesis claims.

This is the archived "Maintenance-Covered Earnings Yield" with a NEG(VOL) term of the *same* ratio appended via SUMRANK; the added stability component is correlated with the level term and will mainly cost coverage (3-year history on (oancf−dp)/lt), making it an incremental tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism.

The cleanest proposal here: expression matches the hypothesis, the sign is unambiguous, and the worst-of-three earnings coverage of current liabilities is a distinct dividend-sustainability conditioner not yet paired with payout yield in the archive (which tested only after-payout cash coverage and liability growth), though it does flirt with well-known payout-safety screens.

The gate is simply the sign-flipped version of the already-tested noncash-current-asset drag term, and because the signed z-score dominates the [0,1] rank the composite mostly re-expresses the well-documented net-operating-asset/working-capital anomaly rather than a genuine value-interaction effect.

Subtracting `dp` from the numerator of the archived "Cost-Scaled Cash Conversion EBITDA Yield" gate is a marginal accounting adjustment to an otherwise identical expression, and the archive already contains a separate `oancf - dp` gate, so nothing new is being tested.

This is a mechanical re-pairing of an already-tested `NEG(dlc/lct)` gate with the most heavily reused value leg (`che`/market cap), and the stated economics — cash pre-committed to debt repayment — would be captured far more directly by a net-cash construction than by a multiplicative gate.

The pairing of an EV-based multiple with noncash operating-asset intensity is the least redundant item in this batch and has a coherent asset-light-versus-clogged-balance-sheet rationale, though it reuses a gate already tested elsewhere in the archive and its incremental content over that result is modest.
